docs.title: whathooks documentation
docs.subtitle: Connect a WhatsApp number, receive inbound messages on your webhook, and send replies through our REST API.
docs.introP1: whathooks lets your clients connect their own WhatsApp number by scanning a QR code. Once linked, the integration works in two directions:
docs.introInbound: <hl>Inbound → webhook.</hl> Every message your number receives is POSTed as JSON to a webhook URL you configure.
docs.introOutbound: <hl>Outbound → API.</hl> You send replies by calling our REST API at <pill>/v1</pill>.
docs.introP2: Your number is connected through a WhatsApp Web link, the same mechanism as WhatsApp's “linked devices”. Reconnection after a dropped link is handled automatically, and each number supports one linked device.
docs.introNote: Because this uses an unofficial WhatsApp Web connection, treat it like a linked device: keep the phone reachable and avoid behavior that could get the number flagged by WhatsApp.
docs.quickstartIntro: Get from zero to a sent message in four steps.
docs.qs1Desc: Sign up and create an organization. All sessions, webhooks, and API keys live under your organization.
docs.qs2Title: 2. Create a WhatsApp session & scan the QR
docs.qs2Desc: Create a session in the dashboard, then open WhatsApp on your phone → <pill>Linked Devices</pill> → <pill>Link a Device</pill> and scan the QR.
docs.qs3Desc: Register an HTTPS endpoint to receive <pill>message.received</pill> and session events.
docs.qs4Desc: Generate an API key to send messages programmatically via <pill>POST /v1/messages</pill>.
docs.connectingIntro: A session moves through a series of statuses as it links and stays online. You can poll a session or subscribe to <pill>session.status</pill> webhooks to track it.

statuses.QR: A QR code is ready to be scanned with WhatsApp.
statuses.CONNECTED: Online and ready to send and receive messages.
statuses.DISCONNECTED: Connection dropped; reconnection is attempted automatically.
statuses.LOGGED_OUT: The device was unlinked; a new QR scan is required.

docs.embedTitle: Embed the QR in your product
docs.embedDesc: Sessions are fully manageable with an API key, so your product can onboard users without ever showing them the whathooks dashboard: create a session, then render the pairing QR in your own UI. <pill>GET /v1/sessions/:id</pill> returns <pill>qrDataUrl</pill> — a ready-to-embed PNG data URI (<imgtag></imgtag>). QR codes rotate, so poll the session while it's in the <pill>QR</pill> status or subscribe to <pill>session.qr</pill> webhooks for fresh codes, and watch for <pill>CONNECTED</pill> to dismiss the QR.
docs.webhooksIntro: When something happens on a session, we POST a JSON body to your configured webhook URL.

events.messageReceived: An inbound WhatsApp message arrived on a connected session.
events.sessionStatus: A session changed status (e.g. CONNECTED, DISCONNECTED, LOGGED_OUT).
events.sessionQr: A new QR code was generated and is waiting to be scanned.

docs.headersIntro: Every delivery includes these request headers:

headers.signature: HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body, formatted as sha256=<hex>.
headers.delivery: A unique ID for this delivery attempt.

docs.envelopeDesc: Every delivery body shares the same envelope: <envtag></envtag>. Below is a full <pill>message.received</pill> delivery:
docs.customizeDesc: Optionally give a webhook mapping rules to reshape data to match your system: rename fields, format dates, and inject fixed values. When rules are set, data contains only the fields you map — the envelope stays the same. Each rule has a target (output name) and either a source (dot path like data.from, also reaching event, sessionId, timestamp) or a fixed value. Add dateFormat to a source rule to format it as a date: iso, unix, unix_ms, or a UTC pattern using yyyy MM dd HH mm ss. Configure it on the webhook in the dashboard, or pass payloadMapping when creating one via API.
docs.signatureDesc: Verify each delivery by computing an HMAC-SHA256 of the <hl>raw</hl> request body using your webhook secret, then comparing it to the <pill>X-Whathooks-Signature</pill> header. Always compare with a constant-time function.
docs.sendingIntro: Send a message with <pill>POST /v1/messages</pill>, authenticated with an API key via the <apikeytag></apikeytag> header. An <bearertag></bearertag> header also works.
docs.sendingTo: The <pill>to</pill> field accepts a bare phone number (digits only, with country code, no <pill>+</pill>) or a full WhatsApp JID. The target session must be <pill>CONNECTED</pill> or the request returns <pill>400</pill>.
docs.sendingSuccess: A successful request responds with the queued message:
docs.apiRefIntro: Base URL in production: <pill>https://api.whathooks.com/v1</pill>. Dashboard requests use a <hl>JWT</hl> (from <pill>/v1/auth/login</pill>), while programmatic requests use an <hl>API key</hl>.
docs.err401: Missing or invalid credentials (JWT or API key).
docs.err400: The session is not <pill>CONNECTED</pill>, or the request body is invalid.
docs.errWebhooks: Delivery requests time out after 10 seconds. For now we make a single delivery attempt per event — automatic retries are coming.
docs.agentsCallout: Building with an AI coding agent? Give it the whole API in one markdown file: <link>whathooks.app/llms.txt</link>
docs.payloadNotes: <pill>type</pill> is uppercase (<pill>TEXT</pill>, <pill>IMAGE</pill>, <pill>AUDIO</pill>, <pill>VIDEO</pill>, <pill>DOCUMENT</pill>, <pill>STICKER</pill>, <pill>LOCATION</pill>, <pill>CONTACT</pill>, <pill>UNKNOWN</pill>). <pill>data.timestamp</pill> is unix seconds (the WhatsApp message time); the envelope <pill>timestamp</pill> is the ISO delivery time.
docs.mediaDesc: For media messages, <pill>media</pill> carries a signed download link (expires after 1 hour — download promptly, or re-fetch the message via <pill>GET /v1/messages</pill> for a fresh link). <pill>text</pill> holds the caption, if any:
